title: ManifestResponse
description: Complete command tree for an agent to discover all available commands, their flags, exit codes, contracts, and examples in a single call, without iterating --help per subcommand.

schema_version.description: Version of the ManifestResponse schema itself. Increment the major when field shape changes in a breaking way.

framework_version.description: Version of the CLI framework or tool binary.

etag.description: Stable content hash of the manifest. Changes only when command registrations change. Agents pass this back via --etag to receive a cache hit instead of recomputing the full manifest.

commands.description: Flat map from dot-separated command path to CommandEntry. 'deploy.rollback' is the rollback subcommand of deploy. Every registered command appears here, including built-ins.

dependencies.description: External runtime dependencies the tool declares (REQ-O-031). tool doctor checks each entry.

flags.description: Global options: flags every command accepts, before or after the command path, keyed by flag name without leading --. A CommandEntry.flags map never repeats a name or short alias listed here. Sourced from REQ-F-079.

exit_codes.description: Shared exit-code table every command inherits. A CommandEntry.exit_codes lists only codes absent from this table or whose entry differs; the command's effective table is this map overlaid with its own. Hoisting the framework codes here keeps the manifest small for agents that read it whole.

description.description: One-sentence summary of what the command does.

aliases.description: Alternative names this command can be invoked with.

danger_level.description: Mutation risk level. safe: read-only; mutating: creates or modifies state; destructive: permanently deletes or irreversibly modifies state. Sourced from REQ-C-002.

required_scopes.description: Minimal permission strings the command needs from the active credential, most critical first. Empty when no auth is required. Sourced from REQ-C-029.

flags.description: Command-local flags: map from flag name (without leading --) to FlagEntry. Global options live in the root flags map and are never repeated here. Sourced from REQ-C-015.

exit_codes.description: Map from exit code integer (as string key) to ExitCodeEntry. Sourced from REQ-C-001. When the manifest has a root exit_codes table, this map holds only the command's additions and overrides; tool <cmd> --schema always prints the effective table in full.

output_schema.description: JSON Schema draft-07 object describing the shape of the command's data payload on success. Agents use this to validate responses and detect schema drift. Sourced from REQ-C-015.

output_formats.description: Format values accepted by --format beyond the framework defaults (json, jsonl, tsv, plain). Omit when only defaults are supported. Sourced from REQ-O-049.

examples.description: Complete invocations that demonstrate the command. Agents copy these verbatim as starting points.

subcommands.description: Dot-separated paths of direct child commands. Resolve each via the top-level commands map.

option_placement.description: any: global options may appear anywhere and local options anywhere after the command path, including among positionals. strict: every option, global or local, must precede the first positional because everything from the first positional on is forwarded verbatim; -- also ends option parsing. Sourced from REQ-C-027.

interactive.description: True if the command may prompt for input in a TTY context; --yes and --non-interactive are then registered. Sourced from REQ-C-005.

has_network_io.description: True if the command makes outbound network connections or long blocking I/O calls; --timeout is then registered. Sourced from REQ-C-012.

steps.description: Ordered step names a multi-step command executes. Responses report completed, failed, and skipped steps by these names. Sourced from REQ-C-008.

spawns_background_process.description: True if the command starts a child process that outlives the invocation. Sourced from REQ-C-010.

cleanup_command.description: Exact command that stops the background process this command starts. Sourced from REQ-C-010.

max_lifetime_seconds.description: Maximum seconds the background process runs before the framework may terminate it. Sourced from REQ-C-010.

filesystem_side_effects.description: Every filesystem location the command may write to. Sourced from REQ-C-011.

secret_env_vars.description: Environment variable names that supply secret values for this command. Sourced from REQ-C-016.

platform.description: Supported operating system names such as linux or darwin. Absent means all platforms. Sourced from REQ-C-018.

required_tools.description: External binaries the command invokes, mapped to the minimum version each needs. Sourced from REQ-C-018.

subprocess.description: How the command builds arguments for a child binary. Sourced from REQ-C-019.

headless_supported.description: Auth commands only: true when the command can authenticate in non-TTY mode without a pre-acquired token. Sourced from REQ-C-021.

token_env_vars.description: Auth commands only: environment variables that supply a pre-acquired token. Required when headless_supported is false. Sourced from REQ-C-021.

async.description: True when the command returns a job descriptor instead of waiting for completion. Sourced from REQ-C-022.

job_descriptor_schema.description: JSON Schema for the job descriptor returned in data by an async command. Sourced from REQ-C-022.

requires_editor.description: True when the command opens $EDITOR or $VISUAL unless an alternative flag is supplied. Sourced from REQ-C-023.

non_interactive_alternatives.description: Flag names, without leading --, that bypass the editor. Required when requires_editor is true. Sourced from REQ-C-023.

gui_operations.description: Display operations the command performs, such as browser_open or desktop_notification. Sourced from REQ-C-024.

headless_behavior.description: How gui_operations behave in headless mode. Sourced from REQ-C-024.

config_write_scope.description: Scope of configuration files the command may write. Sourced from REQ-C-025.

requires.description: Conditional argument dependency rules, evaluated in order. Sourced from REQ-C-026.

streaming_default.description: True when the command streams JSONL by default; --no-stream returns a single envelope. Sourced from REQ-O-004.

safe_default.description: True when the command runs in dry-run mode unless --live is passed. Sourced from REQ-O-048.

type.description: Scalar type of the flag value.

required.description: True if the flag must be provided for the command to proceed.

description.description: What the flag controls, including valid range or format constraints.

default.description: Value used when the flag is omitted. Omit this property (do not set null) when there is no default.

enum_values.description: Exhaustive list of accepted values. Present only when type is 'enum'.

short.description: Single-character shorthand (e.g. 'n' for --dry-run). Omit if none exists.

pattern.description: Anchored regular expression the value must match. Mutually exclusive with pattern_type. Sourced from REQ-C-020.

pattern_type.description: Built-in validation preset for resource identifiers. Mutually exclusive with pattern. Sourced from REQ-C-020.

description.description: One-line description of what this example demonstrates.

command.description: Full invocation string an agent can use verbatim.

path.description: Template or glob for paths the command writes.

ttl_seconds.description: Seconds until the path is considered stale. Omit when permanent.

clearable_with.description: Exact command that removes this path.

user_controlled_args.description: Flag names whose values are passed to the child process as arguments.

hardcoded_args.description: Argument fragments the framework always passes verbatim.

ConditionalRule.description: One conditional argument dependency. Exactly one of the three shapes applies.

if_flag.description: Flag whose value triggers the rule.

if_value.description: Value of if_flag that makes then_required mandatory.

if_flag.description: Flag whose presence triggers the rule.

prohibited.description: Flags that are forbidden when if_flag is present.

if_flag.description: Flag whose absence triggers the rule.

default.description: Default applied to target_flag when if_flag is absent.

name.description: Dependency name, such as terraform or node.

check_command.description: Exact command that prints the installed version.

version_regex.description: Regular expression whose first group extracts the version from check_command output.

fix_command.description: Exact command that installs or upgrades the dependency.
